label: Received esse adds nothing to the essence-only derivation of finitude in perfection
paraphrase: Premise-free, over every grades frame. Explanandum: whatever is not its own being lacks some pure perfection. (1) Essence-only: if each being has in act only what its nature admits, and a nature other than being itself excludes some pure perfection, the explanandum follows. (2) Reception: if whatever is not its own being has its esse received in its nature, and received esse gives only what the nature admits ('limitatum ... ad capacitatem naturae recipientis', De ente cap.4), and the same nature premise holds, the explanandum follows. (3) The reception premises imply the essence-only premise on every being that is not its own being. Both derivations need the nature premise. Reception is not needed for this explanandum. That is not a claim that reception is false.
